{{Quote|So, if the Qrephs had a seat on the committee, they could influence which beacons to repair&mdash;and where to place new ones. And even if they failed to win the vote, they would know the committee's plans.|Omad Kaeg, speculating on why the Qreph brothers sought his founder's share in the miners' cooperative|<ref name="Crucible" />}}
The '''RiftMesh Committee''', informally known as the ''''Mesh Committee''', oversaw the operation of the [[RiftMesh]], a communications network serving the [[Chiloon Rift/Legends|Chiloon Rift]]<ref name="Crucible" /> in [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]].<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> The body directed repairs and expansion of the network, with representation and voting rights granted to holders of a founder's share in the [[Chiloon Rift miners' support cooperative]].<ref name="Crucible" />
In [[45 ABY]], the [[Columi/Legends|Columi]] brothers [[Craitheus Qreph|Craitheus]] and [[Marvid Qreph]] ordered the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] [[Scarn]] to pressure [[Asteroid tug|tug]] [[Captain/Legends|captain]] [[Omad Kaeg]] into surrendering his founder's share. The attempt failed, but Kaeg and his associate [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] suspected the brothers sought the share to gain influence over the RiftMesh Committee and track the placement of RiftMesh beacons, so as to keep their secret [[Base Prime|operation]] in the Chiloon Rift hidden.<ref name="Crucible" />
 
==Behind the scenes==
The RiftMesh Committee was referenced in the [[2013]] [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] novel [[Crucible (novel)|''Crucible'']], written by [[Troy Denning]].<ref name="Crucible" />
